# build_game_hash_files

[← Command index](README.md)

Record hashes of each selected game's files in the per-subcategory hash file.

## Synopsis

```
build_game_hash_files [options]
```

## Description

For each selected game, hashes every file under the game's directory and merges the
records into the subcategory's hash file in the game metadata repository
(`Hashes/<supercategory>/<category>/<subcategory>.json`). Files whose entries are
unchanged are skipped, so re-running only hashes what is new or modified.

The game directory is taken from `-i` if given, otherwise from the game's place under
`-b`, otherwise from the gaming folder of the `-l` locker (the Local locker when `-l`
is omitted). Records include the encrypted name, hash and size computed with that
locker's passphrase, so they match what an encrypted remote locker holds.

Games are listed from the locker when `-l` or `-b` is given, and from the JSON files
in the metadata repository otherwise. With `-d`, entries for files that no longer
exist under the locker's gaming folder are removed afterwards, once per subcategory.

## Options

### Input

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-i, --input_path <input_path>` | Directory to hash instead of the game's locker directory. |

### Selection

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-u, --game_supercategory <game_supercategory>` | Supercategory of the games to hash. Default: `Roms`. Allowed: `Assets`, `Emulators`, `Roms`, `DLC`, `Updates`, `Tags`, `Saves`, `Setup`, `Installs`. |
| `-c, --game_category <game_category>` | Category of the games to hash; all categories when omitted. Allowed: `Computer`, `Microsoft`, `Nintendo`, `Other`, `Sony`. |

PlayStation 3`, `Sony PlayStation Network - PlayStation 4`, `Sony PlayStation Network - PlayStation Portable`, `Sony PlayStation Network - PlayStation Portable Minis`, `Sony PlayStation Network - PlayStation Vita`, `Sony PlayStation Portable`, `Sony PlayStation Portable Video`, `Sony PlayStation Vita`. |
| `-l, --locker_type <locker_type>` | Locker whose gaming folder holds the files and whose passphrase is used for the encrypted fields; Local when omitted. When given, games are listed from this locker. Allowed: `All`, `Local`, `Hetzner`, `Gdrive`, `External`. |
| `-m, --generation_mode <Custom\|Standard>` | How games are selected: `Standard` walks the selected categories, `Custom` takes exactly the given category and subcategory. Default: `Standard`. Allowed: `Custom`, `Standard`. |

### Behavior

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-d, --delete_missing` | After hashing, remove entries for files that no longer exist in the locker. |

### Common options

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-v, --verbose` | Enable verbose mode. |
| `-p, --pretend_run` | Do a pretend run with no permanent changes. |
| `-x, --exit_on_failure` | Enable exit on failure mode. |
| `--no-preview` | Skip the preview confirmation prompt. |

## Examples

### Hash a platform from the local locker

```bash
build_game_hash_files -c Nintendo -s "Nintendo Switch" -l Local
```

### Hash and drop entries for deleted files

```bash
build_game_hash_files -c Nintendo -s "Nintendo Switch" -l Local -d
```

### Hash from a locker copy mounted elsewhere

```bash
build_game_hash_files -c Nintendo -s "Nintendo Switch" -b /mnt/backup/locker
```

### Show what would be hashed without writing

```bash
build_game_hash_files -c Sony -s "Sony PlayStation 2" -l Local -p -v
```

## Notes

- Choose the `-l` locker that matches the content being hashed; its passphrase determines the encrypted fields.
- `-i` is used as the directory of every selected game.
- The supercategory defaults to `Roms`; pass `-u` to hash DLC or updates.
